symptom: A Starlark rule could not see the .jar files in userlib/ and vendorlib/: jar_dependencies() lists only the Maven dependencies module settings declare, and jar_files() was undefined, so one library on the classpath in two versions went unseen.
cause: The jars are files beside the .mpr, not model data, so nothing the catalog builds held them and no builtin read the file system.
insight: Read them at call time from the project folder rather than adding a catalog table: they change without the .mpr changing, so a cached catalog would answer stale. The project folder reaches the linter through the backend's Path() (an optional interface on the reader), so no lint entry point needed a new argument. Split name and version at the LAST '-digit', not the first: log4j-1.2-api-2.17.1 and guava-32.0.1-jre both need it. Measured on CitrusGrove: 65 userlib + 14 vendorlib jars, matching ls, and the duplicate-version rule found real conflicts the Marketplace modules ship (guava android/jre across the two folders, seven netty libraries 4.1.77 vs 4.1.94, slf4j-api 1.7.36 vs 2.0.0). Some .RequiredLib markers name a jar that is not there; they are ignored, not reported as rows.
